items.title: Federal government awards $2.2 million to company led by AI minister’s brother
items.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government has awarded $2.2 million to a company run by AI Minister Evan Solomon’s brother, Jordan Solomon.

items._ogDesc: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government has awarded $2.2 million to a company run by AI Minister Evan Solomon’s brother, Jordan Solomon.
items.body:
OTTAWA – Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government has awarded $2.2 million to a company run by AI Minister Evan Solomon’s brother, Jordan Solomon.

Natural Resources Canada announced the funding for Ecostrat on Thursday. The company’s connection to the AI minister was raised by the Conservatives in Question Period Monday.

Ecostrat works in the biomass industry with the goal of building a “global bioeconomy.” Its president and CEO is Evan Solomon’s brother, Jordan Solomon.

“The Liberals aren’t even hiding any more the amount of self-dealing that’s going on. We’ve gone from art dealing to self-dealing,” said Ontario Conservative MP John Brassard.

“Why are hard-earned tax dollars being used to grease the palms of well-connected Liberal insiders and family members?”

Energy Minister Tim Hodgson responded that the company has been a “delivery partner” with Natural Resources Canada (NRCAN) since 2018. He added that the federal government is working with Ecostrat to implement recommendations from a forestry task force.

“The project was assessed by the department officials according to terms and conditions of the Forest Innovation Program and was appropriately dispersed,” Hodgson told members of Parliament in Question Period.

  • How to set CTV News as your preferred source on Google

The AI minister’s spokesperson Leela Polushin said in a statement to CTV News that Evan Solomon “proactively disclosed all of his relationships to the Ethics Commissioner, including on this matter.”

She added that he “has fully followed the Commissioner’s advice and pre-emptively recused himself from related Cabinet discussions to avoid any potential conflict of interest.”

“He has not been involved in any conversations or decisions related to Ecostrat,” Polushin said.

The Conflict of Interest Act requires public office holders to publicly disclose the recusal and provide “sufficient detail to identify the conflict of interest that was avoided.”

The AI minister’s office initially declined to say whether his recusals were disclosed to the ethics commissioner. Late Monday his spokesperson said the minister has disclosed all recusals to the Ethics Commissioner.

In a separate statement, Jordan Solomon said his work with Natural Resources predates his brother’s time in office.

“I have never discussed my business interests or funding applications with my brother or anyone in his office,” he said. “My brother and I have respected both the spirit and the intent of Canadian ethics and lobbying laws and have not discussed the subject of my company’s lobbying.”

In addition to the $2.2 million awarded last week, Jordan Solomon said his company has previously received a total of $2.77 million in funding.

According to the federal press release issued for last week’s funding announcement, the $2.2-million funding is meant to establish a pan-Canadian network of up to 15 “bioeconomy development opportunity zones.” The purpose of which is to identify areas where commercial-scale manufacturing facilities could be built that can convert local organic waste and biomass into low-carbon fuels, chemicals and everyday materials. Examples of biomass include forestry sector byproducts like sawdust and woodchips.

“Ecostrat is an established organization that certifies regions for their readiness to host bioproduct facilities and helps connect them with global investors and developers,” Hodgson’s spokesperson Carolyn Svonkin said.

“As is standard practice for funding decisions of this type, no Cabinet minister, including Minister Hodgson and Minister Solomon, was involved in the funding decision.”

In a press release issued last week, Ecostrat said the $2.2 million would support a national awards program for forest regions trying to attract new investments. Through the program, the company said forest regions from across Canada can apply and 15 will be selected to receive a Bioeconomy Development Opportunity Zone Rating.

Such a rating “spotlights a region for project developers and investors worldwide,” the company said.

On Parliament Hill, the Conservatives described the spending as “self-dealing for Liberal friends and insiders.”

“Why is this self-dealing happening while the people the prime minister is governing over are suffering?” Brassard asked Hodgson in Question Period.

“This was a specific recommendation of the forest industry task force, a task force that represented all stakeholders,” Hodgson responded.

“This is how we’re going to reform our forest products industry.”

items.title: What Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO means for investors
items.description: News of Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia sent the stock market soaring Monday morning, with shares of the technology company up roughly 30 per cent after a volatile 11 days.

items._ogDesc: News of Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia sent the stock market soaring Monday morning, with shares of the technology company up roughly 30 per cent after a volatile 11 days.
items.body:
TORONTO - News of Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia sent the stock market soaring Monday morning, with shares of the technology company up roughly 30 per cent after a volatile 11 days.

“It was quite a turnaround for the stock. And I think it came at a very opportune moment as well,” said Colin Cieszynski, portfolio manager and chief market strategist with SIA Wealth Management.

“To a certain extent, the shares would probably have bounced back a little bit today. But I think this announcement… led to this explosive rebound that we’ve seen.”

Cieszynski says the rebound is good news for Canadian investors as the stock is included in many exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and mutual funds that sit in RRSPs, TFSAs and other investment accounts.

“Anybody who has anything that is invested in the United States likely owns Nvidia. It’s one of the highest weighted stocks in the United States,” he said.

Less than two weeks ago, Huang stepped down from the company he co-founded after reports of at least two extramarital affairs, one with a woman who U.S. intelligence believes is a Chinese spy.

Nvidia makes advanced microchips that are essential for artificial intelligence infrastructure, and Huang’s relationship sparked major national security concerns.

‘Every confidence in Jensen’

On Monday, Nvidia’s board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as president, CEO and board member.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company.”

Jones’ statement goes on to address the national security concerns raised by Huang’s affair.

“In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”

Just last week Jones told investors the board did not intend to reinstate him. Huang still faces investigations from both the government and the company itself.

“I see it as a ridiculous decision that the board made,” said Richard Powers, who teaches corporate governance at the University of Toronto.

“I don’t understand it at all. No one is irreplaceable. And the board… did not have a succession plan. There was their first failure.” he said.

U.S. President Donald Trump has been a vocal supporter of Huang, whom he counts as a close friend and has spent the last 10 days pushing Nvidia’s board to reinstate him.

“The investigation showed he had bad judgement, having to do with somewhat unrelated incidents, but he did nothing wrong,” Trump told CNBC on Monday following news of Huang’s reinstatement.

Still, the decision has drawn bipartisan criticism with some U.S. lawmakers accusing Trump of prioritizing the stock market over national security.

“The President is selling out our national security to keep the stock market high,” Democratic Sen. Ruben Gallego wrote on social media.

Republic Sen. John Curtis wrote on social media that he has many questions about the investigation and what was behind the board’s decision. “Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board? And on what basis did the board conclude there was no risk?”

Huang is scheduled to appear for closed-door, transcribed interviews on Dec. 1, before three House committees, including the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the House Select Committee on China and the House Intelligence Committee. He is also expected to testify at an open hearing of the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3.

items._ogDesc: New legislation tabled in the legislature Monday allows Alberta to appoint a Crown entity that could participate in natural gas transmission.
items.body:
New legislation tabled in the legislature Monday allows Alberta to appoint a Crown entity that could participate in natural gas transmission.

The province says the current natural gas transmission system (NGTL), owned by TC Energy, is fully subscribed until 2029 and there is uncertainty around its capacity beyond 2030.

“Under these conditions, gas sellers can’t sell, gas buyers can’t buy,” said Energy Minister Brian Jean at a press conference. “Our current transmission infrastructure has failed to keep pace with Alberta’s growth and our ambitions.”

Jean went on to say the Natural Gas Infrastructure Act will give the province the tools to plan, encourage competition and support the development of natural gas infrastructure to best serve Albertans.

While the province is looking to get its natural gas out to the marketplace, the minister said he wants to guarantee Albertans the first chance to reap the benefits.

“We want to make sure Albertans who are facing a lot of bills right now, that natural gas, which is the backbone to our energy and our jobs and just about everything else, is affordable,” said Jean. “As we move forward, we’ll see whether or not industry replies to the needs.”

He added that a Crown entity would only participate as a last resort.

“Alberta’s gas collection and transmission systems, the current NGTL system, was originally built by the government,” said Jean. “With this legislation, we are putting the framework in place to support responsible growth and make the most of our province’s extraordinary potential.”

The act also allows the province to designate critical natural gas infrastructure systems. Future projects deemed critical will still be subject to regulatory, environmental and Indigenous consultation requirements.

Last week, TC Energy announced plans to expand its pipeline network with a 370-kilometre pipeline that stretches west to east called the Alberta Growth Connector, which would add a preliminary billion cubic feet per day of new capacity.

The Calgary-based company has invested more than $15 billion in its NGTL system.

Jean said he’s been in talks with TC over the last few weeks.

“They’re a great company and we’re looking forward to working with them to take advantage of what we have as a natural gas asset, which is an amazing opportunity for us if we move forward together,” said the minister. “We’re looking at the natural gas that goes outside of Alberta and the natural gas system that’s outside of Alberta, and we’re hoping to work with our partners to make it a better system.”

In a letter to the province obtained by CTV News Edmonton, TC Energy said its integrated NGTL-ATCO system provides the lowest cost for Albertans.

“We are concerned the government’s proposed policy direction could have significant, material and negative consequences for Albertans,” said the letter signed by François Poirier, TC Energy’s president and CEO.

“As the government’s own analysis acknowledged in the now-public cabinet brief, it could result, among other things, in increased costs for Alberta families and businesses and expose taxpayers to significant financial risk.”

TC Energy suggests that overriding integration would create significant market instability.

“We struggle to see how we can progress the new offering of more than 1.3 billion cubic feet per day announced on Nov. 16, if legislation overrides the integrated NGTL-ATCO system.”

In September, a report to the premier’s cabinet was leaked, recommending the province make headway on legislation to create two Crown corporations in an effort to meet the demand for oil production and AI data centres.

During her radio program “Your Province Your Premier,” Danielle Smith said it was “unlikely” the government would launch a Crown corporation to build out natural gas pipelines.

Alberta has an estimated 130 trillion cubic feet of natural gas reserves and produces about 60 per cent of Canada’s natural gas.

items.title: U.S. stocks surge and recover half of last week’s plunge after Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia’s CEO
items.description: Nvidia led a thunderous rally on Wall Street Monday following the surprise return of Jensen Huang as the chip company’s CEO.
items.content: <media:description type="plain"><![CDATA[Trader Robert Charmak, left, works on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange in New York, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. (AP Photo/Yuki Iwamura)]]></media:description><media:credit role="author" scheme="urn:ebu">Yuki Iwamura</media:credit>
items._ogDesc: Nvidia led a thunderous rally on Wall Street Monday following the surprise return of Jensen Huang as the chip company’s CEO.
items.body:
NEW YORK — Nvidia led a thunderous rally on Wall Street Monday following the surprise return of Jensen Huang, the charismatic and flawed booster for the entire artificial intelligence industry, as the chip company’s CEO. U.S. stocks recovered just over half their brutal loss from last week, which was one of their worst since the 2008 financial crisis.

The S&P 500 surged 4.7 per cent in a demonstration of how much the U.S. stock market depends on just one industry. Rallies for beaten-down AI stocks sent the Nasdaq composite up a market-leading 6.5 per cent, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped nearly 1,450 points, or three per cent.

Even before Wall Street opened for the day, trading in the futures market suggested U.S. stocks were set to halt the seven-day losing streak that dragged the S&P 500 more than 10 per cent below its all-time high set last month. Then came the bombshell about Huang’s return to Nvidia, even though its board is still investigating whether he was the target of a foreign spy and created any national-security concerns. That kicked the rally into overdrive.

  • S&P 500 market updates here

Nvidia’s stock surged 31.5 per cent and finished just shy of its best day since 2000, close to when the dot-com bubble peaked. That followed its plunge of nearly 23 per cent last week, though it’s still below where it was before Huang’s scandal initially broke.

Stocks closely tied to Nvidia rocketed higher. CoreWeave, a company that buys Nvidia chips and then rents out access to them over the cloud, shot up 22.3 per cent.

Other stocks in far-flung industries that have benefited from the AI boom likewise recovered some of their losses. GE Vernova, which is helping to power AI data centers, rose 8.2 per cent following last week’s drop of nearly 13 per cent. Caterpillar, whose sales of equipment have benefited because of the construction boom around AI, climbed 7.2 per cent after sinking 15 per cent last week.

  • Latest updates on artificial intelligence news here

How AI-related stocks do matters incredibly for workers’ 401(k) accounts because Nvidia and other chip stocks have grown into some of Wall Street’s largest and most influential. Coming into the day, a 1 per cent swing for Nvidia’s stock carried more of an effect on the S&P 500 than a one per cent move for all but two of the 500 companies in the index.

Monday’s rebound for the S&P 500 was its best day since April of 2025, which is when U.S. President Donald Trump paused most of his tariffs announced on “Liberation Day” that had sent stock markets reeling. Trump may have had direct influence on this most recent surge as well.

He told CNBC in an interview Monday, “I believe my intervention was very important” in convincing Nvidia’s board to reinstate its co-founder. Less than a week ago, Nvidia had rejected an offer by Huang to return as CEO.

Trump said his administration assured Nvidia there were no national security concerns about Huang’s return.

To be sure, AI stocks and the broader U.S. market have been prone to extreme reversals since the summer, not only week to week but even hour to hour. Monday’s strength could easily give way to more losses because of the long list of worries dogging the industry.

Beyond general concerns that AI stock prices shot too high and entered into a bubble, worries remain that a Democratic-controlled Congress and statehouses across the country could increase regulations on the AI industry. High interest rates in the bond market are meanwhile making it more difficult to borrow money to pay for the AI build out.

But on the upside for the market, big U.S. companies continue to deliver big growth in profits, at least for the moment. Businesses in the S&P 500 are on track to report an overall jump of nearly 33 per cent in earnings per share for the summer from a year earlier, according to FactSet.

That would be the third straight quarter of growth better than 25 per cent, and stock prices tend to follow the path of corporate profits over the long term.

The risks facing the AI industry could certainly weaken that growth, but analysts at Barclays suggest they should only “make the build out slower and more selective rather than derail it.”

“Markets have been badly bruised by the turmoil of recent weeks, but we do not think the underlying cycle is broken,” Barclays’ Ajay Rajadhyaksha and Amrut Nashikkar wrote in a research report. “Earnings remain strong, global growth is holding up and even if the AI build out slows a little, it is not collapsing. The risks are real, but for now we think they are manageable.”

Oracle rose 12.3 per cent after making a pre-emptive announcement that it had in place all the funding needed to fulfill its deal to provide computing power to OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT.

All told, the S&P 500 rallied 326.78 points to 7,237.17. The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 1,447.98 to 49,595.31, and the Nasdaq composite surged 1,471.82 to 24,089.56.

In stock markets abroad, European indexes climbed more than 1 per cent following a weaker finish in Asia. South Korea’s Kospi fell 3.3 per cent due in part to drops for its big stocks tied to the AI economy, but those moves came ahead of Huang’s return to Nvidia.

  • Latest updates on investing here

In the bond market, the yield on the 10-year Treasury inched up to 4.93 per cent from 4.92 per cent late Friday.

Yields got an upward push as investors felt less need to herd into investments seen as safer.

At the same time, they felt a downward push due to falling oil prices. Brent oil fell 3.6 per cent to US$86.68 per barrel. It’s been yo-yoing between US$72 and US$114 since the United States and Israel attacked Iran in February.

Stan Choe, The Associated Press

AP Business Writers Michelle Chapman, Elaine Kurtenbach and Chan Ho-him contributed to this report.

items.body:
TORONTO — Canada’s main stock index rose nearly 900 points on Monday, while U.S. markets also surged higher after a string of negative moves at the end of last week.  

The rebound came as Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, returning him to the post he resigned from following an admission of an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. 

The S&P/TSX composite index was up 891.59 points at 34,081.44.  

  • Real-time TSX market updates here

In New York, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 1,447.98 points at 49,595.31. The S&P 500 index was up 326.78 points at 7,237.17, while the Nasdaq composite was up 1,471.83 points at 24,089.56.  

Anish Chopra, managing director with Portfolio Management Corp., said that Monday’s rally was being largely driven by Huang’s return.

“That’s really triggering a broad recovery in stocks related to AI and you’re seeing that positive sentiment spill into Canadian markets where gold and mining shares are also moving upwards,” he said.

The December gold contract was up US$136.00 at US$3,651.40 an ounce.

“The TSX is getting a double boost from both stronger gold prices and renewed enthusiasm for technology that’s spilling over from the U.S., and those are two very powerful drivers for Canadian equities today,” Chopra said.

  • Latest updates on artificial intelligence news here

How AI-related stocks do matters incredibly for the broader North American market because Nvidia and other chip stocks have grown into some of Wall Street’s largest and most influential. Coming into the day, a one per cent swing for Nvidia’s stock carried more of an effect on the S&P 500 than a one per cent move for all but two of the 500 companies in the index.

AI stocks and the broader U.S. market have been prone to extreme reversals since the summer, not only week to week but even hour to hour.

Despite Monday’s rally, Chopra said investors still have longer-term questions about AI valuations, spending and the future profitability of the sector.

“There are still concerns about the profitability in the AI space, the fact that interest rates have risen, the fact that growth could be slowing, the fact that valuations in the AI sector are quite high,” Chopra said.

“I don’t think today takes away from that.”

  • S&P 500 market updates here

Beyond general concerns that AI stock prices shot too high and entered into a bubble, worries are also high that a Democratic-controlled U.S. Congress and statehouses across the country could increase regulations on the AI industry.

The Canadian dollar traded for 69.59 cents US compared with 69.81 cents US on Friday.  

The January crude oil contract was down US$3.24 at US$80.17 per barrel. 

Daniel Johnson, The Canadian Press

items.body:
CALGARY — Oil and gas service firms say improving market conditions and a more supportive political climate are expected to bolster Canadian drilling activity next year, but labour shortfalls could threaten that momentum.

Industry advocacy group Enserva has released its annual state of the industry report, which calls for an increase in the number of wells drilled in 2027 versus this year.

But it flags competition for workers as a major challenge at a time when artificial intelligence data centres and major infrastructure projects draw from the same talent pool.

  • Latest updates on company news here

Bradley Fedora, president and CEO of Trican Well Service Ltd., says the prospect of “hyperinflation” in the cost of labour and materials is what scares him most.

Thomas Alford, president of completion and production services at Precision Drilling, told reporters at the event that it can take up to eight years to train up a competent drill rig staffer, and the industry has been so unstable in recent years that it’s been hard for those workers to get that consistent job experience.

Gurpreet Lail, Enserva’s president and CEO, says the sector needs to work hard to attract and keep talent as data centre developments offer big paycheques to tradespeople and perks that have until now been “unheard of.”

Lauren Krugel, The Canadian Press

items._ogDesc: Two Iraqi Boeing 747s, including a luxury aircraft once associated with Saddam Hussein, are being offered for sale after spending 35 years stranded in Tunisia. The jets are listed for US$900,000 each, but buyers will face significant costs and the aircraft have been declared unairworthy.
items.body:
Two Boeing 747s once linked to Saddam Hussein’s regime are being offered for sale for less than the price of a luxury sports car, after spending more than three decades abandoned at a Tunisian airport.

Iraqi Airways is seeking US$900,000 for each aircraft, or $1.8 million for both, as it attempts to find buyers for the aging jets that have been sitting in the desert since 1991.

A luxury jet fit for a dictator

The more notable aircraft is a Boeing 747SP, registered as YI-ALM and named Al-Qadissiya. Built in 1982, the plane was configured as a VIP aircraft for Hussein’s government, featuring a private bedroom, conference room and a luxurious lounge with sleeper seats.

The aircraft is one of just 45 Boeing 747SPs ever manufactured.

The second aircraft, a Boeing 747-200, was used for commercial passenger and cargo operations, with seating for 330 passengers, including 45 in first class.

Their distinctive Iraqi markings were covered with white paint, but decades of exposure to the desert climate have gradually revealed the original green livery underneath.

Why the planes never returned home

Both aircraft arrived at Tozeur-Nefta International Airport in southwestern Tunisia on Jan. 1, 1991, shortly before the Gulf War.

  • How to set CTV News as your preferred source on Google

Iraqi Airways initially sent technicians to maintain the VIP aircraft twice a year. However, international sanctions, disputes involving Kuwait and mounting airport fees eventually left the planes stranded.

By 2020, parking charges alone had reportedly exceeded $5 million.

A costly deal for potential buyers

The jets are being sold without technical guarantees and have been declared unairworthy by Tunisian authorities.

Potential buyers must provide a $180,000 deposit for each aircraft and pay the remaining amount within five days of an accepted offer. Transport, customs, taxes and additional parking fees will also be their responsibility.

Bids will be reviewed between Dec. 21 and Jan. 5, with the sale expected to conclude by Jan. 7, 2027.

If no buyer emerges, Iraqi Airways says it may scrap the historic aircraft.

items.title: Doug Ford ‘very confident’ Canada could see trade deal with U.S. soon
items.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith expressed optimism Monday that Canada could see a trade deal reached with the U.S. before the end of the year.

items._ogDesc: Ontario Premier Doug Ford and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith expressed optimism Monday that Canada could see a trade deal reached with the U.S. before the end of the year.
items.body:
Ontario Premier Doug Ford and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith expressed optimism Monday that Canada could see a trade deal reached with the U.S. before the end of the year.

The two premiers took part in a wide-ranging fireside chat moderated by BNN Bloomberg’s Amanda Lang at the Toronto Region Board of Trade Monday and were asked how optimistic they are about the prospects for a deal.

“I think if there’s going to be a deal, there’s a very high chance it would be before the end of the year, because just knowing the type of personality that we have in the in the White House, I don’t think he wants to be perceived as having been pushed into a deal by the Democrats who are going to be sworn in on Jan. 3,” Smith said.

“So it seems to me that this is the window for him to say that whatever strategy he was employing with Canada, that it worked, and here’s a big beautiful deal that works for America, and so that’s what I’m hoping for.”

Weighing in, Ford said he’s “very confident” about the prospects for a deal.

“We saw what happened at the midterms, right? The Republicans got annihilated. I think a big part of it — yeah, you could say the war in Iran and the oil — and it’s tariffs.”

He said U.S. businesses, as well as Canadian ones, have been battered by the tariffs.

“A tariff on Canada was no more than a tax on the United States, the people of the U.S.,” Ford said. “We saw prices go up here, and it comes down to what people want, right in this room, everywhere in their own personal life, but in business, they want certainty. They want stability.”

Still, Ford reiterated he would not be in favour of a deal that leaves key industries behind.

“We’re going to continue focusing on the right deal. I say I’d rather have no deal than a bad deal, and so we’ll see if President Trump has shifted after the midterms,” Ford said.

“Maybe he’s thinking, ‘I’ll take a bullet out of the Dems’ gun if we make this deal,’ but only if the auto sector and the steel sector and manufacturing sector come to me after they see a proposal and say ‘we’re good with this, we can grow and survive,’ and then I’m all in.”

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in an interview on Fox News Sunday that the U.S. is “fairly close” to agreeing on a trade deal with Canada.

Smith says deal shouldn’t hinge on French Netflix

Smith also said that getting a trade deal would allow the two countries to move forward with a “bigger conversation that we need to have,” namely joint defence projects like the Golden Dome missile defence system.

“It’s not really about whether or not the French language programming in Quebec gets priority on Netflix. That’s not really what the big conversation with Canada and the U.S. should be,” Smith said.

“The big conversation is: Do they want the Golden Dome or not? Do they want Arctic security or not? If we’re going to build the Golden Dome, we’re going to have to build a broadband infrastructure across our northern Arctic community, as well as at the south, and then we’re going to have to connect it with data centers so that we have the ability to intercept anything that might be coming over.”

She said it’s “frustrating” the tacks sometimes seem to get sidetracked on “in some cases, quite small issues.”

The two premiers discussed a number of topics, from energy infrastructure to interprovincial trade barriers.

While the premiers have tried to tear down interprovincial trade barriers to bolster their economies in the face of U.S. tariffs, Smith said it has been challenging to do so without any exemptions, citing a trade deficit between the two provinces when it comes to alcohol products as an example.

TORONTO — The Children’s Place and Gymboree are liquidating all of their Canadian stores while the brands’ parent company hunts for a buyer.

The two children’s apparel retailers have 56 stores across nine Canadian provinces, documents filed with an Ontario court by The Children’s Place, Inc. and its affiliates earlier this month show.

The locations are due to sell off their inventory by Feb. 28 at the latest -- an effort meant to help the company pay off the mountain of debt that led to its insolvency proceedings.

All sales are final, except for purchases made between Oct. 23 and Nov. 6. Both brands’ websites said they will continue accepting gift cards for a “limited time” but will soon share a cutoff date for using the vouchers.

However, if a buyer is found for some of the Canadian stores, the court filings say those locations could be removed from the liquidation sales and perhaps run by a new owner. Bids for the company and its assets are due by Dec. 9 with an auction scheduled for Dec. 11, but any transaction would be subject to court approval.

The sell-off comes as the retailers, known for offering affordable kids clothing, are simultaneously liquidating U.S. stores. An Ontario court has previously recognized the U.S. bankruptcy protection proceedings for the stores’ owner.

The Secaucus, N.J., company founded in 1969 blamed its need for court protection on declining consumer demand for value-oriented children’s apparel, persistent inflation, tariffs on imported goods and intense competition and promotions from retailers and e-commerce brands.

Court documents show the company recorded a net loss of $84.1 million for the first half of its fiscal 2026. Sales for the 26 weeks leading up to Aug. 1 declined by 15.4 per cent to $457 million.

In fiscal 2025, Canadian sales were $92.5 million, making up 7.7 per cent of the company’s consolidated net sales, the documents say. Some $52 million of that cash was generated through brick-and-mortar locations, while the rest came from e-commerce.

The company had been trying to stave off creditor protection for a few years. In its court filings, it said it refinanced over the last two years and reviewed its store footprint and inventory to uncover savings.

  • Latest updates on company news here

Court documents say these efforts generated “meaningful liquidity,” but ultimately, “did not offset the magnitude of the revenue decline and operating losses.”

As of Nov. 6, court records show the company owed $381.6 million through various loans and credit facilities to Wells Fargo, Crystal Financial and Mithaq Capital SPC.

Mithaq Capital, an investment company for Saudi Arabia’s Al Rajhi family, has a 61.1 per cent equity stake in The Children’s Place and Gymboree’s parent company, court records show. Mithaq initially purchased a 50 per cent stake in 2024 and later increased its holdings.

The Children’s Place and Gymboree empire includes 512 stores in North America and 323 international distribution points. They are serviced by a distribution centre in Fort Payne, Ala., and a third-party facility in Mississauga, Ont.

Court records also say the company had 749 employees in Canada at the end of October. Most of them had part-time roles at Children’s Place and Gymboree stores.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 23, 2026.

Tara Deschamps, The Canadian Press

items._ogDesc: Canadian household debt hit $3.3T in September as mortgage growth fell to a 25-year low, while consumer credit ran hot on rising distress borrowing.
items.body:
Canadian household debt is slowing in growth, but it doesn’t appear to be voluntary deleveraging. Statistics Canada (StatCan) data shows household credit climbed in September, though mortgages are contributing less. The segment grew at one of the slowest paces in a quarter-century, even as consumer credit took off alongside rising distress borrowing.

Canadian Household Debt Hits $3.3 Trillion Even As Growth Slows

Annual growth of Canadian household credit.

Source: StatCan; Better Dwelling.

Canadian household debt climbed 0.3% (+$9.4 billion) to hit $3.3 trillion in September, 3.7% (+$119.3 billion) higher than last year. It’s a sharp deceleration from the 4.6% annual growth reported this time a year ago, suggesting household borrowing is slowing. Even at a slower pace, adding over $119 billion in a single year is hardly deleveraging. Households are just lightly tapping the brakes.

Canadian Mortgage Credit Growth Slows To Lowest Pace In 25 Years

Annual growth of Canadian mortgage credit.

Source: StatCan; Better Dwelling.

Mortgage growth appears to be the big drag here. Outstanding mortgage credit rose 0.2% (+$4.9 billion) to $2.47 trillion in September, 3.5% (+$82.6 billion) from last year. This is the slowest annual growth for mortgage credit since mid-2001. In an economy as housing-dependent as Canada’s, a quarter-century low in mortgage expansion signals that buyers are either tapped out or stuck on the sidelines.

Distress Borrowing Keeps Consumer Credit Running Hot At $847 Billion

Annual growth of Canadian non-mortgage household credit.

Source: StatCan; Better Dwelling.

One area of credit growth that continues to run hot is consumer credit. Households grew non-mortgage debt by 0.5% (+$4.5 billion) to $847.0 billion in September, up 4.5% (+$36.7 billion). While slower than August, the annual growth of this segment has been higher than usual over the past few years, sustaining levels the country hasn’t seen since mid-2010. Healthy credit growth can sometimes be a sign of strong consumers, but this isn’t one of those times.

Credit reporting bureaus are increasingly attributing growth to distress borrowing. Firms like TransUnion have noted that more borrowers are carrying higher balances as they use credit to make ends meet. Mortgage borrowers aren’t much better, with the bureau also explaining that a rising share of mortgage debt is due to accumulating balances, not originations.

Slowing headline growth may look like restraint on the surface, but it’s a more ominous sign. There are few signs of relief ahead, as the market expects higher borrowing costs.

items.title: M3’s Bernard talks CMAs, importance of recognizing top performers
items.description: Broker network backs the Canadian Mortgage Awards as brokers gain ground in a tough market
items.content: <p>Broker network backs the Canadian Mortgage Awards as brokers gain ground in a tough market</p><img src="https://cdn-res.keymedia.com/cms/images/us/074/0388_639275163379725593.png" alt="" style="max-width:240px" />
items._ogDesc: Broker network backs the Canadian Mortgage Awards as brokers gain ground in a tough market
items.body:
The Canadian Mortgage Awards (CMAs) finally arrive this week – and as the event’s social media sponsor, M3 Financial Group is backing the brokers, lenders, and service providers shortlisted across multiple categories.

The event, set to take place at Rebel Toronto on November 25, will celebrate its 20th anniversary this year. Luc Bernard, chairman and chief executive officer of M3, told Canadian Mortgage Professional that paying tribute to the industry’s best performers was an essential part of ensuring the sector goes from strength to strength.

“We feel that it is of utmost importance to celebrate the mortgage broker industry and recognize the top performers,” he said. Being in a room with the sector’s highest achievers, he said, “obliges us to continue elevating our work year after year.”

The event draws nominations from brokers, brokerages, lenders, underwriters, business development managers (BDMs), and industry service providers across the country. Nominations closed in August, with the shortlisted Excellence Awardees published last month.

Brokers can be recognized regionally, with separate awards for Eastern Canada (Quebec and Ontario), the Maritimes and Atlantic Canada, and Western Canada, or by specialty – with awards for alternative, private lending, reverse mortgage and commercial brokers.

Brokerages and teams compete by size, alongside awards for national broker networks, national brokerages and new brokerages. On the lending side, BDMs and underwriters are recognized in both prime and specialist (alternative and private) categories. Industry service providers, innovators and employers of choice round out the field.

All you need to know about the award categories

Several awards put the spotlight on people. Twelve brokers are shortlisted for Young Achiever of the Year, 11 for The MCAN Award for Woman of Distinction, and nine for The REMIC Award for Finfluencer of the Year, (see CMP's full list of 2026 Canadian Mortgage Awards excellence awardees here).

The fields vary in size. The regional broker awards each have 10 or 11 shortlisted brokers, while the private lending and commercial categories have seven each, the reverse mortgage category three, and the National Broker Network of the Year category four.

Sponsors have also put their names on individual awards, including The EQ Bank Award for Broker of the Year – Reverse Mortgages and The Grechi Carter Professional Corporation Award for Broker of the Year – Commercial. The Haventree Bank Award for Lifetime Achievement, the programme's highest honour, has no shortlist and will be announced only on the night.

Brokers shine in challenging times

The industry’s top performers have shone in a challenging market this year, one that’s brought the importance of mortgage brokers into even sharper focus.

The ongoing trade war with the US, and price pressures caused by the US-Iran conflict, have weighed against the housing market outlook for 2026 as affordability challenges and rising interest rates also leave their mark.

But brokers are coming to the fore in turbulent times that have also seen a wave of mortgage renewals in 2025 and 2026 at much higher rates than the original contract.

Overall broker market share reached 38% last year, according to Mortgage Professionals Canada’s (MPC’s) most recent consumer survey – a jump of six percentage points from the year before.

Nearly two in five Canadians took out their most recent mortgage through a broker in 2025, a new high for the channel, with the share climbing to 48% among recent first-time buyers.

For M3, a key focus of the year has been broker education, with the aim of equipping brokers to be “the best that they can be for future Canadian homeowners.”

Bernard said the night is also a reminder of the bigger goal. “Let’s all work together to grow this industry, allowing more Canadians to trust brokers with the biggest purchase of their lives,” he said.

items.description: As the CMAs mark 20 years, RFA Financial's VP duo reflects on philanthropy, brokers, and 2027
items.content: <p>As the CMAs mark 20 years, RFA Financial's VP duo reflects on philanthropy, brokers, and 2027</p><img src="https://cdn-res.keymedia.com/cms/images/us/074/0388_639310575802854874.png" alt="" style="max-width:240px" />
items._ogDesc: As the CMAs mark 20 years, RFA Financial's VP duo reflects on philanthropy, brokers, and 2027
items.body:
For RFA Financial, returning as a sponsor of the 2026 Canadian Mortgage Awards is not simply a matter of brand visibility — it is an expression of values the Toronto-based lender says are foundational to how it operates.

The awards, presented by Canadian Mortgage Professional, return to Rebel Toronto on November 25 for their 20th anniversary, recognising outstanding work across 26 categories spanning broker, brokerage, lender, and industry segments.

The 2026 edition arrives at what CMP has described as one of the most structurally significant moments in the country's recent mortgage history, shaped by a record renewal wave and persistent affordability pressure from coast to coast.

Among the sponsors backing this year's programme is RFA Financial Inc., the parent company of RFA Mortgage Corporation and RFA Bank of Canada — the firm's prime and alternative lending subsidiaries, respectively.

RFA Mortgage Corporation is sponsoring the Excellence in Philanthropy & Community Service award, a category that Cheryl Buhs, VP of National Sales (Prime) at RFA Financial, says carries particular meaning.

"Our sponsored award, the RFA Award for Excellence in Philanthropy & Community Service, is especially meaningful to us," Buhs told Canadian Mortgage Professional. 

"Giving back to the communities we serve is an integral part of RFA's culture, and it's something we work to champion across the industry."

The recognition of community service within a business-focused awards programme reflects a broader shift visible at the CMAs in recent years.

Buhs said RFA sees its sponsorship as part of a continuing effort to hold up those contributions for wider visibility.

"Supporting this award is one small way we can shine a light on the people making a difference across our country and encourage others to do the same," she said.

Raising the bar across the industry

Frank Giacomini, VP of National Sales (Alternative) at RFA Financial, echoed the view that industry recognition has a practical effect on standards.

"Recognizing the hard work of our peers keeps our industry moving forward," said Giacomini.

"When we celebrate great work, we inspire everyone to raise the bar and find new ways to serve our communities and make homeownership more accessible for Canadians."

The 2026 Canadian Mortgage Awards is proud to recognize the Excellence Awardees of the RFA Award for Excellence in Philanthropy & Community Service, presented in partnership with RFA. #MortgageAwardsCA Book a table: https://t.co/tR6Q1ATWEp https://t.co/u8ZkpHqm5z — Canadian Mortgage Professional Magazine (@CMPmagazine) November 18, 2026

Looking ahead to 2027

On the year that is wrapping up and the one ahead, Buhs offered a note of gratitude to the brokers and partners who have kept the relationship with RFA active through a demanding market cycle.

"It's been another great year of connecting with our industry partners, and we're grateful for the relationships and collaboration that make RFA what it is," she said.

"Thank you to everyone who continues to put their trust in us. We're excited for what 2027 holds and look forward to building on this year's momentum together."

Giacomini added that RFA's focus heading into the new year remains unchanged: deepening its value to the broker channel.

"RFA is always working to be the preferred lending partner for brokers, and this year has been no different," he said.

"As we close out 2026 and head into 2027, our focus remains the same — finding ways to better serve our broker partners and their clients."

Both executives extended congratulations to the nominees and finalists assembled for November 25.

"We're constantly impressed by the standard set for our industry, and we're honoured to celebrate with you," said Buhs.

items.title: Why Tru Cooperative Bank is backing the Canadian Mortgage Awards
items.description: Tru Cooperative Bank's SVP on sponsoring the CMAs, broker relationships, and a national expansion that crossed the Rockies
items.content: <p>Tru Cooperative Bank's SVP on sponsoring the CMAs, broker relationships, and a national expansion that crossed the Rockies</p><img src="https://cdn-res.keymedia.com/cms/images/us/074/0388_639310566057090312.png" alt="" style="max-width:240px" />
items._ogDesc: Tru Cooperative Bank's SVP on sponsoring the CMAs, broker relationships, and a national expansion that crossed the Rockies
items.body:
When Tru Cooperative Bank agreed to sponsor this year's Canadian Mortgage Awards (CMA), the decision was grounded in something more straightforward than marketing arithmetic.

The federally regulated credit union, formerly known as First West Credit Union, has worked alongside mortgage brokers in British Columbia for more than 23 years — and sponsoring the industry's benchmark recognition event is, in the words of its senior vice-president of pricing and national expansion, Sundar Ramanathan, CFA, (pictured top) a chance to say thank you.

"We have worked with mortgage brokers in B.C. for more than 23 years, and mortgage brokers have played a huge role in our growth," he told Canadian Mortgage Professional.

"Now, as we take our broker business across Canada as a federal credit union, sponsoring the Canadian Mortgage Awards is a chance to say thank you and celebrate the people who've helped us prove that there's an important place for cooperative banking in this industry."

The 2026 CMAs mark the programme's 20th anniversary, a milestone that coincides with one of the most structurally consequential periods in the Canadian mortgage market's recent history. 

The gala takes place November 25 at Rebel Toronto, spanning 23 competitive categories that recognise outstanding work from broker specialists in private lending and reverse mortgages to the teams and technology shaping the market's future.

Results are announced at the awards show and simultaneously published on the CMA website, with coverage in CMP magazine and across its digital channels. mpamag

Raising the bar

Ramanathan makes no distinction between celebrating excellence and improving the broader market.

As a lender that operates on cooperative principles — member-owned, profit-averse in the conventional sense — Tru Cooperative Bank regards recognition events as instruments of collective advancement.

"Mortgages are ultimately a people business," Ramanathan said.

"Great brokers bring advice, trust, and expertise to one of the biggest financial decisions Canadians make. As a cooperative, we believe we're stronger when we help each other succeed. Recognising excellence celebrates the people setting a high standard and raises the bar for the whole industry."

The 2026 Canadian Mortgage Awards is proud to partner with Tru Cooperative Bank in recognizing the Excellence Awardees of the Tru Cooperative Bank for National Brokerage of the Year. #MortgageAwardsCA Book a table: https://t.co/TCt6mK5FV9 https://t.co/M2N4rjG8LI — Canadian Mortgage Professional Magazine (@CMPmagazine) November 19, 2026

A landmark year for Tru

For Tru Cooperative Bank itself, 2026 has been a year of institutional transformation.

First West Credit Union announced on April 1 that it was officially a federally regulated credit union operating under the new legal name Tru Cooperative Bank, with regulatory oversight transferring from the BC Financial Services Authority to the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), placing it under Canada's federal banking regulatory framework.

With this transition, Tru Cooperative Bank became the fourth federally regulated credit union in Canada since federal legislation introduced in 2012 enabled credit unions to operate nationally. 

The broker expansion followed quickly. In May, the organisation announced the expansion of its Mortgage Broker Centre into Ontario through a strategic partnership with MCAP, a Canadian mortgage lender and servicer.

Less than four months after becoming a federally regulated credit union and just 77 days after expanding into Ontario, Tru Cooperative Bank had already exceeded $100 million in approved mortgage volume. 

Provincial growth continued through the year. The move to extend the institution's broker reach deepened a national expansion that gained substantial momentum in Ontario, with Alberta, Saskatchewan, and Manitoba following, and Atlantic Canada identified as the next target market, according to Ramanathan. 

"Our message to brokers is simple: we're here for the long term," Ramanathan said.

"We have 80 years of history behind us, and while our national broker business is new, we aren't. We want to earn brokers' business for the long term by listening, staying competitive and consistent, and being a lender they genuinely like working with."

items.title: Montrealers could pay 9.8 per cent more for municipal taxes, document reveals
items.description: A budget summary on the City of Montreal’s website, which has since been taken down, indicates that Montrealers could be paying 9.8 per cent more for their municipal taxes in 2027.
items.content: <media:description type="plain"><![CDATA[An undated photograph of Montreal homes.]]></media:description>
items._ogDesc: A budget summary on the City of Montreal’s website, which has since been taken down, indicates that Montrealers could be paying 9.8 per cent more for their municipal taxes in 2027.
items.body:
A budget summary on the City of Montreal’s website, which has since been taken down, indicates that Montrealers could be paying 9.8 per cent more for their municipal taxes in 2027.

When asked about the proposed increase, Montreal Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada’s administration would not confirm the details of the document.

The document explains that the city plans to present a balanced operating budget of $8 billion, focusing on “well-maintained streets and infrastructure, safe neighbourhoods and high-quality services.”

“For fiscal year 2027, City Council is limiting the increase to the general property tax to three per cent of City Council’s expenses, for both residential and non-residential properties, which corresponds to the inflation rate observed for the Montreal metropolitan area,” the file reads.

However, a breakdown shows an increase of:

  • 2.6 per cent for general property taxes;
  • 1.5 per cent for the water tax;
  • (0.3 per cent - decrease) for debt taxes;
  • 5.1 per cent for the infrastructure maintenance tax.

Additionally, Montrealers would be expected to pay 0.7 per cent for service taxes and 0.1 per cent for investment taxes, which the chart purports to add up to 0.9 per cent.

Combined, the total is an increase of 9.8 per cent.

Montreal officials are justifying the large increase by pointing to a “significant investment shortfall in the maintenance of our infrastructure.”

“The city is creating a new reserve for infrastructure maintenance and renewal,” the document states.

It explains that for 2027, $139 million is being earmarked for cash payments allocated to the reserve “to meet the growing needs related to the maintenance and renewal of its infrastructure.”

As for the projected increases to the water tax, the city says it plans to add $70.6 million to the local water reserve, “in particular to continue implementing the Montreal Water Strategy.”

‘Difficult decision’

While at an announcement for Montreal’s bid to host the Defence Bank, Martinez Ferrada spoke about the city’s impending budget, which is set to drop on Tuesday.

“I have made a sincere commitment to addressing inflation. The decision I made today is extremely difficult for [several] reasons,” she said.

“But failing to make the decision we made would jeopardize all our other commitments, including making housing and homelessness top priorities, as well as ensuring we have infrastructure befitting a major city and providing essential services to our citizens.”

She argued that Montrealers can no longer “pass onto future generations the burden of decisions we should have made many years ago.”

10-year program

The City of Montreal is also proposing a 10-year capital investment program (PDI) for 2026–2035 totalling $23.4 billion, again with an emphasis on the aging infrastructure.

“Maintenance of existing assets accounts for 76.5 per cent of investments, while the development, acquisition and installation of new equipment, the construction of new infrastructure, and the upgrading of existing infrastructure to current standards account for 23.5 per cent,” the document notes.

The city says it is reducing the portion of the PDI allocated to development “to direct more resources toward the infrastructure crisis and the maintenance needs that have accumulated over the years.”

items.title: First National's residential mortgage chief to retire in December
items.description: EVP announces he'll end an illustrious career next month
items.content: <p>EVP announces he'll end an illustrious career next month</p><img src="https://cdn-res.keymedia.com/cms/images/us/074/0388_639310556202175047.png" alt="" style="max-width:240px" />
items._ogDesc: EVP announces he'll end an illustrious career next month
items.body:
Scott McKenzie, executive vice president of residential mortgages at First National Financial LP in Toronto, Ontario, has announced he will retire at the end of December, drawing to a close one of the longest and most consequential careers in the history of Canada's non-bank lending sector.

McKenzie joined First National in 1989 as its fifth employee, months after co-founders Stephen Smith and Moray Tawse established the firm.

He went on to assume a mandate that cut across the full scope of residential mortgage operations — both origination and credit — an unusually broad combination in the industry that made him a defining figure in how the lender built and maintained its relationships with brokers nationwide.

First National distributes its residential mortgages exclusively through the broker channel.

Read more: Macklem to exit Bank of Canada as successor search begins

From the fifth employee to $100 billion in mortgages

Under his oversight, First National's residential portfolio grew to $100 billion in mortgages under administration (MUA), according to the company, while the team under his leadership expanded to more than 1,000 employees. That trajectory ran in close parallel with the broader rise of the broker channel in Canada.

According to Mortgage Professionals Canada, the share of Canadians obtaining their mortgage through a broker climbed to 38%, up six percentage points from the year prior, with first-time buyers driving the sharpest gains.

McKenzie captured his perspective on that relationship in a 2024 message to mark the company's 35th year in the broker channel: "We are grateful that mortgage brokers give First National the chance to compete, the opportunity to serve and the encouragement to grow and innovate. To all of our partners, thank you for your support."

Read more: Montreal fintech nesto names SVP to accelerate operational growth

A year of leadership transition

McKenzie's retirement is not the only succession underway at First National this year. In March, the company announced that president and chief executive Jason Ellis would also step down by year's end, following more than 22 years at the firm.

First National has not named a successor for McKenzie's role, nor provided a timeline for doing so.

items.description: RECO revokes Luxury Homes World and broker of record after complaints over frozen buyer deposits
items.content: <p>RECO revokes Luxury Homes World and broker of record after complaints over frozen buyer deposits</p><img src="https://cdn-res.keymedia.com/cms/images/ca/046/0319_637100048227359663.jpg" alt="" style="max-width:240px" />
items._ogDesc: RECO revokes Luxury Homes World and broker of record after complaints over frozen buyer deposits
items.body:
The Real Estate Council of Ontario (RECO) has revoked the registrations of a Scarborough real estate brokerage and its broker of record following multiple complaints that approximately $500,000 in buyer deposits was held against transactions that failed to close.

Luxury Homes World Inc., located at 700-305 Milner Avenue, Scarborough, Ontario, and its broker of record, Inthiran Swamy, had their registrations cancelled on November 17. Neither the brokerage nor Swamy may now trade in real estate in the province.

Accounts frozen and registrations revoked

RECO moved first with a freeze order on November 10, covering all accounts associated with Luxury Homes World, including its real estate trust account, under the Trust in Real Estate Services Act, 2002 (TRESA).

The step was taken to safeguard consumer funds and prevent further unauthorized movement of money.

The enforcement followed multiple complaints linked to approximately $500,000 in submitted deposits for transactions that did not complete.

RECO confirmed the investigation is continuing and that further regulatory action may follow. The regulator noted the freeze order was unrelated to its mandatory annual financial filings program, which all approximately 3,800 registered Ontario brokerages were required to complete as of October 1.

Buyers who paid deposits to the brokerage are urged to contact RECO directly; the regulator administers a consumer deposit insurance program that may provide recourse for lost funds.

The Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA) has imposed conditions on the insurance agent licence of Victor Ferreira following a settlement over administrative penalties that went unpaid for more than six years. https://t.co/meZLsXW9k6 — Canadian Mortgage Professional Magazine (@CMPmagazine) November 11, 2026

Part of a wider pattern of enforcement

The Luxury Homes World case extends a string of RECO enforcement actions that have unsettled Ontario's real estate sector over the past 12 months. \

In February, RECO took action against four Save Max brokerages in Mississauga after a forensic review found approximately $2.7 million had been improperly withdrawn from trust accounts.

Those actions followed RECO's December 2025 freeze of accounts at Scarborough-based HomeLife Today Realty Ltd., where a shortfall of approximately $580,000 was uncovered, and the August 2025 collapse of iPro Realty Ltd., which exposed a $10 million shortfall and triggered a government-ordered audit of RECO's regulatory approach.

As RECO pushes through its eight-point modernization plan in the wake of those failures, its administrator and acting chief executive, Jean Lépine, has framed the enforcement surge in unambiguous terms.

"It is about ensuring that a small number of bad actors do not undermine the integrity of the entire profession," Lépine said in March at the Ontario Real Estate Association's annual general meeting in Ontario.

The Ontario Real Estate Association (OREA) has backed the tougher oversight. As RECO set an October deadline for mandatory annual brokerage financial filings, OREA president Kim Fairley welcomed the direction.

"OREA is thrilled to see RECO and the Government of Ontario heed our calls for increased financial oversight and trust account reforms for brokerages, which will go a long way towards building back trust in the regulator," Fairley previously said.

items.title: Fengate, Capital Developments Buy TAS Leslieville Site Out Of Receivership For $16M
items.description:
Another development site formerly owned by Toronto-based developer TAS has been sold under receivership, according to filings in Ontario Superior Court and transaction details obtained by STOREYS.

The site is 880 Eastern Avenue and 80 Knox Avenue in the Leslieville neighbourhood of Toronto, a few blocks west of Ashbridges Bay and Woodbine Park.

TAS acquired 80 Knox Avenue in 2020 with a first-ranking mortgage in the principal amount of $10.3 million that was provided by Canadian Mortgage Servicing Corporation (CMSC) — a subsidiary of Canadian Mortgage Capital Corporation (CMCC) — and acquired 880 Eastern Avenue via a $4.32 million vendor take-back mortgage provided by Michael & Michael Auto Body Ltd.

In September 2022, the CMSC loan was then amended to facilitate the acquisition of 874 and 876 Eastern Avenue for $2.5 million “to have additional adjacent lands available for the benefit of the intended development,” according to court documents.

For the site, TAS was planning a 12-storey building with 184 rental units and 10,000 sq. ft of commercial space on the ground floor — the numbers have been updated multiple times — and the project was once set to become Toronto’s first net-zero mid-rise residential building.

The properties were beneficially owned by TAS through 880EA Corp. and 874EA Corp. while TAS LP 3 served as the guarantor of the CMSC loan.

The Insolvency

According to CMSC, the loan matured in February 2025, TAS stopped making interest payments in July 2025, and also failed to make property tax payments. It also took out another mortgage from Toronto-based private equity real estate investment firm KingSett Capital in March 2025 without obtaining consent from CMSC. (KingSett Capital was also a lender to TAS on their Labatt Village project.)

CMSC issued a formal demand for payment in August 2025 and said it was owed $10,734,679.39 as of August 13, 2025, with interest continuing to accrue. After the borrowers could not repay the debt, CMSC initiated the receivership proceeding.

In its application, CMSC noted there was a “protracted sale effort” pertaining to the properties that began around May 2024 and ran for about a year. The property was listed by Dan Rogers, Jeff Lever, Reilly Hayhurst, and Mike Murray of Cushman & Wakefield as a “partnership or sale opportunity,” according to the sales brochure.

CMSC said the previous sale attempt was unsuccessful and that they wanted to have the project placed under receivership so it can be sold free and clear of all claims.

“I believe that an immediate sale will maximize the value of the Secured Properties for the benefit of all stakeholders,” said CMSC’s Managing Director in a September 2025 affidavit. “Moreover, the situation is an ongoing risk whereby CMSC’s security position may erode.”

The Sale Process

The project approved for 880 Eastern Avenue and 80 Knox Avenue. (SvN Architects, TAS)

The development site was placed under receivership on September 17, 2025, and the court-ordered sales process commenced shortly afterwards. Although the court-appointed Receiver opened up the process to other brokers, they ultimately re-engaged Cushman & Wakefield due to the work they had already done.

The Receiver said there was “significant market interest,” with 31 parties signing confidentiality agreements and 8 parties submitting bids by the December 9 deadline. However, the Receiver and Cushman were “dissatisfied with all offers received” and decided to open a new sales process, this time including the possibility of a vendor take-back (VTB) mortgage funding a portion of the purchase price.

Although Toronto-based developer Capital Developments did not submit an offer in the initial sale process, it remained interested and eventually submitted an offer in the second round, which was accepted by the Receiver on February 9. The sale agreement was amended in March, April, and July before it was finalized and then approved by the Ontario Superior Court on September 23.

“In conjunction with the closing, the Receiver proposes to assign the VTB to CMSC and M&M in its entirety,” said the Receiver in a report. “In the case of M&M, the Receiver proposes to assign the portion of the VTB up to the value of its debt, inclusive of interest as at the date of closing.”

“While an ideal scenario would have resulted in a cash only purchase price for the Real Property, the Receiver and Cushman & Wakefield are of the view that the current environment required structured finance by way of the VTB to maximize the purchase price and provide the highest recovery to affected stakeholders,” the Receiver added.

Notably, 874 and 876 Eastern Avenue were left out of the sale, and the Receiver said there were no bids at any point for the two properties.

The Project

The purchase agreement was originally signed by CD Capital Developments (Acquisitions) Limited in February, but the final agreement was instead signed on July 31 by 880 Eastern Limited Partnership.

The final sale price was redacted from court documents, but according to an Altus Group transaction report obtained by STOREYS, 880 Eastern Avenue and 80 Knox Avenue transacted on October 15 for $16,000,000, with $10,250,000 funded in cash and $5,750,000 funded by the vendor take-back mortgage.

On October 27, Fengate Asset Management then announced that it had established a joint venture with Capital Developments, with Fengate managing the investment on behalf of the LiUNA Pension Fund of Central and Eastern Canada and Capital Developments making the acquisition through Address, its rental platform.

“Toronto’s population continues to grow, and the supply of high-quality rental housing has not kept pace,” said Jaime McKenna, President, Fengate Real Estate. “We are thrilled to be partnering with Address, a team that shares our commitment to delivering more housing for our city. Together, we are unlocking new rental supply in Leslieville and creating a connected community where people can live and work, with convenient access to transit, the waterfront and everyday amenities.”

The partners said they plan to develop more than 250 rental units, including affordable rental units, suggesting the project may look different than what was previously approved. Construction is expected to begin in late-2027.

If you’re thinking about building your own palatial home, a vacant White Rock property with an ocean view may be to your liking.

Listed for $8.3 million, the vacant lot in the 13700-block of Marine Drive is described as an “extraordinary opportunity to create an iconic waterfront estate on 1.57 acres along one of White Rock’s most coveted stretches of Marine Drive.”

With large homes on either side, the real estate listing notes that significant site preparation has been completed with custom-home plans available.

A private path leads to the shoreline and an intimate oceanfront viewing deck, the listing describes.

“A rare canvas for a world-class residence shaped by light, landscape and the sea,” the listing by The Partners Real Estate and The Agency White Rock states.

The parcel has been on the market for more than 100 days.

According to BC Assessment, the site had an assessed value, as of July 1 2025, of $6,869,000. That is down from $7,385,000 the previous year.

A recent report from REMAX Canada notes the luxury residential real estate market across Canada demonstrated a regional divide through the first nine months of 2026.

Smaller markets led sales growth, while major metropolitan centres saw buyer hesitation, with the overall luxury market in Greater Vancouver (-17 per cent) and the Greater Toronto Area (-9.4 per cent) recording contractions.

The overall luxury market is defined as homes in the $3 million-plus range.

As far as the so-called “top-tier” of the market, defined as homes $7.5 million-plus, the Greater Toronto area was actually up almost 18 per cent, while Greater Vancouver was down eight per cent.

The report goes on to note, “Greater selection encouraged buyers to negotiate more aggressively, while some sellers who already adjusted their asking prices showed reluctance to make further concessions.”

Time for your cheat sheet on this week’s top stories.

Canadian Real Estate

Canada Is Borrowing $765B. Here’s The Problem We Explained To Parliament

This week, we were summoned to Parliament to present evidence to its finance committee. In our opening statement, we chose to focus on explaining the impact of the scale of borrowing on credit markets and the country’s financial stability. The scale of borrowing requires a significant amount of capital to flow into bonds, pushing the cost of borrowing higher for all borrowers. At the same time, the record investment pouring into those bonds is creating a systemic risk the Bank of Canada has quietly referred to as a “self-reinforcing liquidity spiral.”

An MP Asked What Ottawa’s Borrowing Costs Canadians. Here’s the Math

How much will the Government of Canada’s epic borrowing spree cost Canadians? We crunched the numbers in response to Canada’s finance committee’s questions, and estimate it would push the 5-year bond yield 13 to 26 basis points higher. This would cost households up to $8.7 billion in extra interest on their personal loans, but it doesn’t end there. Businesses, and ironically the government of Canada, would also incur higher borrowing costs due to “crowding out.”

Canadian Real Estate Prices Not Expected To Rise Through 2030: BMO

Canadian home prices have fallen 22.8% from peak, and it’s even sharper after adjusting for inflation. BMO Capital Markets warned that real (inflation-adjusted) home prices have made an even steeper drop, the largest since the 1980s. Elevated mortgage rates and weak wage growth are expected to drag prices in real terms through 2030, warns the bank.

Canadian Home Prices Down 23%, Only Reversing 13 Months of Gains

The price of a typical home across Canada slipped 0.3% (-$2.1k) to $649.9k in October. That’s 22.8% below the March 2022 peak, reversing only 13 months of gains. Weak sales and strong inventory suggest the potential for further price declines, but prices still remain out of reach, nearly 4 years after the correction began. The progress—or lack of—emphasizes the scale of exuberance prior to the rate hike shock.

Canadian Inflation Holds At 3.1%, Property Taxes Soar As Arrears Rise

Canadian headline inflation held steady at 3.1% in October, helped by a 2.5% drop in gas prices, though gas prices are still 30.9% higher than last year. October’s CPI also included the annual update for property tax and special charge inflation, which advanced 3.8% year-over-year. While that’s lower than last year, it’s still much higher than the Bank of Canada’s 2.0% average, and comes as property tax arrears in regions like Ontario have surged.

items.title: Flurry of luxury mansion sales this fall in West Vancouver
items.description: Despite the sluggish real estate market, 11 high-end North Shore homes sold for more than $7M between August and October
items._ogDesc: Despite the sluggish real estate market, 11 high-end North Shore homes sold for more than $7M between August and October
items.body:
Even as the broader North Shore real estate market continues to struggle, the high end of the market has been surprisingly active in recent months, with 11 luxury properties selling for between $7 million and $16 million since early August.

The sales include waterfront homes, sprawling estates in West Vancouver’s British Properties and Altamont neighbourhoods, and a contemporary waterfront property in North Vancouver’s Deep Cove.

But while wealthy buyers are still willing to pay millions for the right property, a number of the sales suggest that sellers have had to make significant adjustments to their expectations on prices, with several selling for millions below their original asking prices.

The most expensive sale was a mansion at 1036 Eyremount Dr. in West Vancouver’s British Properties neighbourhood.

The seven-bedroom, 11-bathroom home sold Sept. 26 for $16 million, below its final asking price of just under $18 million, after 33 days on the market.

The nearly 11,400-square-foot home was built in 2020 and features panoramic views of the Vancouver skyline, Mount Baker and the harbour. It had originally been listed for just under $22 million, and was assessed at $8.35 million.

Realtor Derek Grech of The Partners Real Estate in West Vancouver describes that sale as “a bit of an outlier” on a property that cost a lot to build.

Luckily for the seller, “a local guy liked that house,” he said.

The second-most expensive sale was a waterfront mansion at 2878 Bellevue Ave. in West Vancouver.

The 4,200-square-foot, four-bedroom, five-bathroom home sold Aug. 2 for $13.5 million after being on and off the market for about seven years.

Designed by architect Russell Hollingsworth, the 10-year-old home features spa-inspired ensuites and a climate-controlled wine room. The home includes three fireplaces and a 1,200-square-foot crawl space.

The final asking price was just under $14 million, although the home was originally listed in 2019 for just under $17 million. It was assessed at $12.7 million and last sold in 2017 for $13 million.

Another high-profile waterfront sale was a contemporary home at 3478 Marine Dr. in West Vancouver’s West Bay neighbourhood.

The four-bedroom, five-bathroom home sold Oct. 31 for $9.6 million, below its final asking price of $11.8 million, after being listed in July. The two-year-old, nearly 3,700-square-foot home was designed by McLeod Bovell and features exposed concrete and steel and commands sweeping views across Burrard Inlet.

The property had been listed on and off since 2024, when it was originally offered for $18.8 million. Its assessed value was $5.2 million.

Grech said that was another property where the original asking price was out of sync with what the market was prepared to pay.

“I would say that that was an aspirational reach for sure.”

A newly built estate at 1840 Orchard Way in West Vancouver sold Sept. 23 for $9 million, about $4 million below its final asking price, after 44 days on the market.

The six-bedroom, eight-bathroom home spans about 8,000 square feet on a third-acre property. Features include an infinity pool, panoramic ocean views and separate kitchens on the main and lower levels. The one-year-old home was assessed at just under $11 million.

In Altamont, a sprawling estate at 2958 Mathers Cres. sold Oct. 12 for $8.7 million, below its original asking price of $10.5 million.

The 28-year-old, 10,000-square-foot-plus mansion has eight bedrooms and 11 bathrooms and sits on a property of more than three-quarters of an acre. The gated estate includes a swimming pool, hot tub, gym, media room and four-car garage. Its assessed value was $8.75 million.

“A couple of years ago it would have been $11 million,” said Grech. “So it was listed at $8.9 million and sold in 31 days for $8.7.”

Another Altamont property, at 2980 Palmerston Ave., sold Nov. 2 for $8.5 million after five months on the market. The eight-bedroom, eight-bathroom Tudor-inspired home spans about 12,500 square feet and sits on a property of nearly 40,000 square feet.

The estate features mature gardens, an outdoor pool, tennis court and a lower-level entertainment area with a wine cellar, gym, spa and theatre. It had been listed on and off for several years, with an asking price of $14.8 million in 2021.

A waterfront property at 3180 Travers Ave. in West Vancouver’s West Bay sold Sept. 2 for $8.5 million after 83 days on the market. The sale involved a property with plans for an approved but yet-to-be-built 6,400-square-foot waterfront home, designed by Hlynsky + Davis Architects. The land alone was assessed at $8.9 million.

1167 Eyremount Dr. in West Van’s British Properties sold Sept. 7 for $7.5 million, below its asking price of $10 million. The seven-bedroom, 10-bathroom mansion is about 10,500 square feet and sits on a 0.6-acre lot. It had originally been listed for $17.3 million in 2021 and last sold in 2015 for just under $11 million.

In North Vancouver’s Deep Cove, a contemporary waterfront home at 1840 Naomi Pl. sold Sept. 16 for just under $7.4 million after 162 days on the market. The five-bedroom, four-bathroom home, designed by architect Frits de Vries, sits at more than 4,300 square feet and includes an infinity pool and a private dock. It had originally been listed for almost $8.7 million and was assessed at $6.8 million.

A newly built home at 2356 Ottawa Ave. in West Vancouver sold Sept. 27 for $7.2 million after just 12 days on the market, below its asking price of just under $8 million. The five-bedroom, seven-bathroom home spans more than 6,200 square feet and includes a glass elevator, theatre, sauna and outdoor pool. Its assessed value was $6 million.

Rounding out the rush of luxury home sales was a five-bedroom, seven-bathroom home at 1515 Camelot Rd. in West Vancouver, which sold Oct. 22 for $7 million, below its asking price of $8.6 million, after 100 days on the market. The 6,500-square-foot home features an infinity-edge pool, spa, home theatre and wine cellar. It was assessed at $8.2 million and last sold in 2017 for $9.3 million, over $2 million more than it was recently sold for.

It’s important to remember, said Grech, “that house selling in 2017 for $9.2 million in that area was a record.... So there’s lots of price index to fall from that height of the market.”

items.description:
